Theme

Kitchen, meals & drinks · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

kind noun

also variety, sort, type, that sort of thing, that type of person

classical

Cic. Amic. 71: odiōsum sānē genus hominum
Traupman 336
Traupman 399

genus, generis n.

noun, third declension

kind or variety

Other words

  • quālis, quāle — what kind of? what sort of?; of the kind that

    adjective, interrogative and relative, declension · also used · classical · Mart. 12.92.4: sī fīās tū leō, quālis eris?; Traupman 406: what kind of, what sort of, quālis

  • ejus modī (hujus modī) — of that (this) kind, that sort of

    genitive of quality, after its noun · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 5.48: pompā, lūdīs atque ejus modī spectāculīs

    Also written as one word, ejusmodī, hujusmodī.

Examples

  • Quod genus gelātī vīs?

    What kind of ice cream do you want?composed

  • dīc mihi, sī fīās tū leō, quālis eris?

    tell me, if you turned into a lion, what kind of lion would you be?Mart. 12.92.4

  • odiōsum sānē genus hominum officia exprobrantium

    a tiresome sort indeed, people who throw their favours in your faceCic. Amic. 71

  • istīus generis homō

    that type of personTraupman 399

See also ice cream, flavour, sort of, what kind of, such, a man of.
